children.title: Abstract
children.body: We construct an explicit bulk dual in anti-de Sitter space, with couplings of order , for the -singlet sector of QED in space-time dimensions () coupled to scalar fields. We begin from the bulk dual for the theory of complex free scalar fields that we constructed in our previous work, and couple this to gauge fields living on the boundary in order to get the bulk dual of scalar QED (in which the gauge fields become the boundary value of the bulk vector fields). As in our previous work, the bulk dual is non-local but we can write down an explicit action for it. We focus on the CFTs arising at low energies (or, equivalently, when the gauge coupling goes to infinity). For we discuss also the addition of a Chern-Simons term for , modifying the boundary conditions for the bulk gauge field. We also discuss the generalization to QCD, with gauge fields coupled to scalar fields in the fundamental representation (in the large limit with fixed ).

The AdS/CFT correspondence [1, 2, 3] is an equivalence between theories of quantum gravity on asymptotically anti-de Sitter (AdS) space in dimensions, and conformal quantum field theories (CFTs) in dimensions. Since for we do not have any non-perturbative definition of these quantum gravity theories, the correspondence should be viewed as providing a non-perturbative definition for these theories in terms of the corresponding quantum field theories, whenever those are known and well-understood. In many cases of the correspondence the gravitational theories have a classical limit, in which the ratio of the Planck scale to the radius of anti-de Sitter space goes to infinity, and which corresponds to a large limit of some sort in the CFT side. In those cases one can test the correspondence by checking that the semi-classical expansion on the gravity side agrees with the large limit of the corresponding field theories.

gist.html: AdS/CFT defines quantum gravity in AdS by a CFT; large-$N$ limits give its classical limit.

children.body:
A derivation of the AdS/CFT correspondence requires showing that the CFT can be rewritten as a quantum gravity theory, in the sense that its expansion reproduces the corresponding perturbative expansion around some gravitational solution in AdS space. While one can often test this for specific observables, providing such a derivation for the full theory is challenging (see [4, 5, 6, 7] for some recent progress in relating free symmetric orbifold CFTs to string theory on ). In our recent paper [8] we provided such a derivation for the simplest case of the AdS/CFT correspondence – the duality [9] between the -singlet sector of free complex scalar fields in dimensions, and a theory of higher-spin gravity on . Our derivation in [8] followed the methods of bi-local holography [10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15], in its Lorentz-invariant version. We first changed variables in the CFT from the free scalar fields () to their bi-local combinations

(1.1)

which capture all the information about -invariant observables in the theory (at least in flat space). In the large expansion one can write down an action for that reproduces the correlators of the original theory, to all orders in (as discussed in [8], the mapping to the bi-local variables makes sense also for finite but it is more subtle then, and in this paper we only discuss the theory in the expansion). In order to map this to a theory in AdS space, we first expanded the bi-local field in a basis of eigenstates of the Euclidean conformal group . We then showed that the same eigenstates appear in the expansion of transverse traceless fields of spin () living on a fixed space, enabling a one-to-one mapping between these fields and the bi-local (1.1). Using this mapping we rewrote the action of the original theory as an action (with coupling ) for fields in AdS space. This action is explicitly known but is non-local. For a specific choice of the undetermined coefficients appearing in the mapping, the quadratic term in the bulk can be chosen to be local. Since the -singlet sector of free scalars is conjectured [9] to be dual to Vasiliev’s high-spin gravity theory [16, 17, 18], we believe that our action is equivalent to a gauge-fixed version of this theory, in which its fields live on a fixed AdS space-time (as in [19]); the spectrum of physical fields is consistent with this, but the equivalence has not yet been shown.

gist.html: The authors' earlier work rewrote free scalars' singlet sector, via bi-local fields, as an explicit non-local AdS action.

children.title: Collective fields at large N
children.body: In a theory of $N$ fields in the vector representation, every singlet observable can be written through bilinears such as $G(x_1,x_2)=\frac1N\sum_I\phi^*_I(x_1)\phi_I(x_2)$. Jevicki and Sakita showed that one can change variables in the path integral from the $\phi_I$ to these collective fields. The change of variables costs a Jacobian, $\exp[(N-V)\operatorname{Tr}\log G]$ on a lattice of $V$ points, so the whole action becomes proportional to $N$. At large $N$ the path integral is then dominated by a saddle, the free propagator for free fields, and $1/\sqrt N$ fluctuations around it reproduce the $1/N$ expansion, with $1/N$ playing the role of $\hbar$. The collective field has two points, not one, so it has more variables than a local field in $d$ dimensions. The paper's starting point is that a function of two boundary points carries exactly the content of a tower of fields of every spin in $AdS_{d+1}$.

In this paper, we generalize this construction to the -singlet sector of scalar QED – the theory of a gauge field minimally coupled to charged scalar fields, for . In principle this generalization is straightforward, since on the field theory side it just involves introducing a dynamical gauge field and coupling it to -singlet combinations of the scalar fields, and we can in principle do this also on the gravity side. On-shell, local -invariant operators (such as the ones appearing in the coupling to the gauge field) map to the boundary values of the bulk fields on AdS space; however, the construction above requires the off-shell mapping of the local CFT operators to the bulk, and at first sight this seems to be more complicated. In [8] we showed that for and the naive on-shell mapping works also off-shell, and we used it there to derive the dual to the critical (or ) vector model, by coupling a singlet to the spin operator . In this paper we show that the same is true also for and , and also for higher values of . This allows us to write down a simple action for the -dimensional gauge field coupled to the bulk fields; in fact, as may have been expected [20, 21, 22, 23, 24], the gauge field becomes simply the boundary value of the -dimensional vector field . Thus, compared to the original theory of free scalars, the description of QED just involves changing the boundary condition for the bulk vector field , and perhaps adding some boundary terms for it. The boundary terms are required if one wants to describe QED at finite coupling, but they disappear in the low-energy limit, where QED (for ) flows to a conformal field theory (at least at large and to all orders in [25], and perhaps also for all finite values of [26, 27]). In the special case of one can also add a Chern-Simons coupling at level ; when is kept fixed in the large limit, this coupling is translated into a modified boundary condition for the bulk vector field.

gist.html: Local operators of every spin map off-shell to the bulk, so the QED photon becomes the bulk vector's boundary value.

children.title: Gauge fields in AdS and boundary conditions
children.body: A bulk gauge field in $AdS_{d+1}$ has two possible behaviours near the boundary $z\to0$: a constant mode $a_i(x)$ and a mode falling as $z^{d-2}$, whose coefficient is a conserved current $j_i(x)$ of dimension $d-1$. The standard choice fixes $a_i$: it is a source, and the CFT has a global $U(1)$ with current $j_i$. One may instead let $a_i$ fluctuate and integrate over it. In the CFT this couples a dynamical gauge field to $j_i$, gauging the symmetry. For $d<4$ both choices give normalisable modes, and Witten showed that the $SL(2,\mathbb Z)$ action on three-dimensional CFTs with a $U(1)$ maps them into each other; adding a Chern–Simons term gives a mixed condition. These were statements about correlators; the paper derives them from the CFT, off-shell, for scalar QED.

One application of our bulk formalism for QED would be to find classical solutions in the bulk describing monopole operators, and perhaps to use them to compute their correlation functions. As we discuss below, our formalism only includes monopole operators if there is no Chern-Simons coupling for the , and it may be interesting to look for ways to get around this problem so that monopoles in Chern-Simons-matter theories may also be incorporated.

gist.html: The bulk could describe monopole operators as classical solutions, but only without a Chern–Simons term.

children.body: We also generalize our construction to the singlet sector of scalar fields in the fundamental representation of a gauge field (“scalar QCD" [28]), when is kept fixed in the large limit, and for we can again include a Chern-Simons level . The bulk dual is very similar to the QED case, except the bulk fields now transform in the adjoint representation of . Note that this limit is different from the large and fixed limit considered in [29], which is believed to also be dual to a parity breaking higher spin bulk theory. It would be interesting to see if the generalization of our construction to this limit just involves changing boundary conditions, or explicitly changes the bulk interaction terms as a function of (see discussions in [30, 23]). Such a generalization, as well as the inclusion of fermions, would allow us to similarly construct the bulk dual of ABJ theory [31] in its higher spin limit, which could ultimately lead to a connection to string theory and M-theory via the ABJ triality [23, 32].

gist.html: Scalar QCD at fixed $N_c$ works the same way, with adjoint bulk fields; large-$N_c$ Chern–Simons-matter limits differ.

children.body: Finally, our off-shell mapping allows us to construct the bulk dual for the critical or vector model for , as discussed in [33, 34]. This CFT is not unitarity at finite due to complex large instantons [35], but is unitary in the expansion. It would be interesting to study the classical solutions corresponding to these instantons from the bulk perspective using our construction.

gist.html: The off-shell map also gives the bulk dual of the critical vector model in $4<d<6$.

children.body: We begin in section 2 by describing the -singlet sector of scalar QED in bi-local variables, and translating its action to these variables. In section 3 we review the mapping found in [8] between the free scalar theory and the bulk, and extend it to an off-shell mapping for local operators in the CFT. In section 4 we then use this mapping to construct the bulk dual for the -singlet sector of scalar QED, and show that it reproduces the expansion of this theory. Finally, in section 5 we discuss the generalization to scalar QCD.

children.title: A subtlety in restricting to the singlet sector
children.titleHtml: A subtlety in restricting to the singlet sector

children.body: We will be interested in the singlet sector of scalar QED. In general , we can simply restrict to this sector by hand, which has no nontrivial effects on . For and non-zero , we need to be more careful. What we actually do is first restrict the theory of scalars to its -invariant sector, and then couple this sector to the gauge field. We can perform the restriction in a rigorous way [44] by coupling the theory to a Chern-Simons term at infinite level before coupling to the new gauge field, and we will use this to show that monopole operators cannot appear in the singlet sector (as we define it here) when . Thus, for and non-zero our theory is not precisely the same as the -singlet sector of scalar QED (which could have -singlet monopole operators), but we will still call it by this name. In all other cases our theory includes the full -singlet sector of scalar QED.

gist.html: The singlet sector is taken before gauging; in $d=3$ with $k\neq0$ this excludes monopole operators.

children.title: Monopole operators and the topological symmetry
children.body: In a three-dimensional $U(1)$ gauge theory the dual field strength $j^T_i=\frac1{2\pi}\varepsilon_{ijl}\partial_jA_l$ is conserved identically, so the theory has a topological $U(1)_T$ global symmetry. Operators charged under it are monopole operators: they create a unit of magnetic flux through any sphere surrounding their insertion point, much as a 't Hooft line does in four dimensions. In other dimensions the same construction gives operators of codimension three. With a Chern–Simons term at level $k$, Gauss's law ties electric charge to magnetic flux, so a monopole operator of unit flux also carries $k$ units of gauge charge. To be gauge invariant it must then be dressed with charged matter fields. In the paper that dressing is what conflicts with the way the singlet sector is defined.

Let us start by considering the free theory with action in , with global symmetry . We can gauge this by adding a Chern-Simons term for a gauge field , with scalar couplings:

(2.16)

where is the gauge field, is the current, and in the second line we separated out the terms from the gauge field , which couples to the current defined in (2.2). The gauge-invariant operators are then all singlets of , as we want, but the theory is modified by the extra fields, and in particular it has new monopole operators charged under a topological global symmetry generated by the dual of the field strength of . We can then take the limit, which on removes all dynamical effects of the gauging, including the existence of monopoles charged under the , and we obtain precisely the desired restriction to singlets.

A monopole of the photon then carries $k$ units of charge, and any dressing that cancels it is charged under the $U(N)$ gauging, so for $k\neq0$ the theory has no gauge-invariant monopoles. For $k=0$, and for $d\neq3$, monopoles remain.

children.title: Harmonic analysis on the conformal group
children.body: Just as Fourier analysis expands functions on $\mathbb R^d$ in plane waves, harmonic analysis on the Euclidean conformal group $SO(d+1,1)$ expands conformally covariant functions in its irreducible representations. A function of two points can be decomposed into conformal three-point structures with an operator of dimension $\Delta$ and spin $J$ at a third point $y$. children.body: In Poincaré coordinates, $ds^2=(dx^idx^i+dz^2)/z^2$, the boundary is at $z=0$. A scalar field of mass $m$ solving the wave equation behaves near the boundary as $z^{\Delta}$ or $z^{d-\Delta}$, with $m^2=\Delta(\Delta-d)$; a field of spin $J$ behaves similarly with powers shifted by $J$. The bulk-to-boundary propagator is the solution sourced at one boundary point, falling as $z^{d-\Delta}$ times a delta function there and as $z^\Delta$ times a two-point function elsewhere. In the standard dictionary the coefficient of the slower fall-off is the source and that of the faster one the expectation value of an operator of dimension $\Delta$. For a massless spin-$J$ field dual to a conserved current, $\Delta=d-2+J$. The paper uses these propagators also as a basis for expanding bulk fields.

We will first review the bulk action for the free and critical theories, which were derived in [8]. We will then use the off-shell map of single-trace local operators for to show that the bulk QED action is given by a simple deformation of the bulk dual of the free theory. children.body: We start by considering a free theory of scalars with global symmetry . The singlet sector under the subgroup can be translated to the bulk just like the usual free scalar theory, except that now both the singlet bi-locals in the CFT and their dual bulk fields are adjoints under , and the terms in the bulk action are all single traces of products of matrices. We can then construct the bulk dual of scalar QCD by a procedure similar to the one described in the previous sections: gauging (in the CFT), fixing a gauge convenient for the large expansion, mapping the current (which is a singlet) to the bulk using our usual CFT-to-AdS map, and coupling it to the new gauge fields. The main differences from the Abelian case are that now the Yang-Mills and Chern-Simons terms for contain self-interactions of the gauge fields, and that the gauge-fixing now leads to ghosts (in the adjoint of ) which will live on the boundary and couple to the gauge fields there.

gist.html: Bulk fields become $U(N_c)$ adjoints; non-abelian gauge self-interactions and ghosts live on the boundary.

children.body: As with QED, the resulting bulk theory is related to the bulk dual of the free theory by a simple change of boundary conditions for the spin one bulk field (in the adjoint of ). • Context The authors had rewritten free scalars' singlet sector as gravity in AdS, deriving AdS/CFT there. Can a gauge field be added?

brief.html:
AdS/CFT is taken to define quantum gravity in AdS through a CFT, but deriving it means rewriting a whole CFT, to all orders in $1/N$, as a gravitational theory. The authors had done this for the simplest case, the singlet sector of $N$ free complex scalars, dual to higher-spin gravity: through bi-local fields, an explicit non-local action on fixed AdS. Here they gauge the scalars' $U(1)$, which gives scalar QED in $2 The answer is simple: the boundary photon becomes the boundary value of the bulk vector field, so the QED dual is the free dual with that field's boundary condition changed.

The difficulty is that gauging couples the photon to the current inside the path integral. The map from local operators to the bulk must then hold off-shell, as an operator identity, not only inside correlators. The map expands the bi-local and the bulk fields $\Phi_J$ of every spin $J$ in the same basis of conformal representations, and identifies the coefficients. The earlier work had an off-shell identity only for spin zero below four dimensions. The paper extends it to every spin and every $d>2$. A source for a spin-$J$ operator makes the bi-local singular as its points meet, at any $N$, and absorbing the singularity shifts the bulk field's boundary behaviour. Comparing with a bulk source term then gives $S^J(x)=f_{d-2+J,J}^{-1}\lim_{\epsilon\to0}\epsilon^{2-d}\Phi_J(x,\epsilon)$: each single-trace operator is a rescaled boundary limit of its bulk field.

For spin one that operator is the $U(1)$ current, so the photon's coupling becomes a coupling of a boundary field $A_i$ to the boundary limit of $\Phi_1$. Gauge-fixing and Chern–Simons terms do not involve the scalars and stay on the boundary. At infinite gauge coupling and without a Chern–Simons term, $A_i$ acts as a Lagrange multiplier: it sets the current to zero, and $\Phi_1$'s $z^0$ mode becomes dynamical, equal to $A_i$ up to normalisation. In terms of a boundary field strength, the free dual has electric boundary conditions, $\mathcal F_{ij}=0$, and QED magnetic ones, $\mathcal F_{zi}=0$. Correspondingly the vector's physical propagator is replaced by a shadow one, whose boundary condition also depends on the CFT's gauge-fixing parameter $\zeta$. After a field redefinition both $\sigma$ and the photon couple linearly, so the $\mathbb{CP}^{N-1}$ dual is the free dual with alternate boundary conditions for $\Phi_0$ and $\Phi_1$. The paper argues that this reproduces the model's correlators to all orders in $1/N$.

In $d=3$ a Chern–Simons term for the photon can be added at level $k$, with $\kappa=k/N$ fixed at large $N$. It makes the boundary condition mixed, $\mathcal F_{ij}+\frac{2\pi i}{16\kappa}\varepsilon_{ijl}\mathcal F_{zl}=0$, so that the shadow propagator comes in an infinite family labelled by $k$. The singlet sector is defined rigorously by first gauging the scalars' $U(N)$ at infinite Chern–Simons level. For $k\neq0$ a monopole then carries $k$ units of gauge charge, and any dressing that cancels it is charged under that $U(N)$, so no monopole operators remain.

The off-shell map for spin zero, now valid above four dimensions, also gives the bulk dual of the critical $U(N)$ or $O(N)$ vector model wherever it exists at large $N$, for $2 There the auxiliary field $\sigma$ removes the scalar's $z^{d-2}$ mode, so free and critical duals differ only in the bulk scalar's boundary condition, to all orders in $1/N$. For $U(N_c)$ scalar QCD with $N$ fundamental scalars at fixed $N_c$, bi-locals and bulk fields become $U(N_c)$ adjoints, and gauging adds self-interacting gauge fields and ghosts on the boundary. Again the dual is the free one with a changed boundary condition for the spin-one field.

The bulk dual is explicit but non-local: only its quadratic term can be made local, by a choice of normalisation. It is believed, not shown, to be a gauge-fixed form of Vasiliev's higher-spin gravity. The bulk vector has no gauge freedom of its own, and its propagator depends on how the CFT is gauge-fixed. The construction holds in the $1/N$ expansion, and not in the large-$N_c$ Chern–Simons-matter limit, which is expected to have a different dual. Bulk solutions for monopole operators, which the formalism contains only without a Chern–Simons term, are left for future work.

defs.html: The conjectured equivalence between quantum gravity on asymptotically anti-de Sitter space in $d+1$ dimensions and a conformal field theory in $d$ dimensions, its boundary. Lacking another definition of the gravity side, the paper treats the CFT as defining it, and derives the bulk theory from the CFT.

The part of a theory made of operators invariant under a symmetry group, here $U(N)$ or $SU(N)$ acting on the $N$ scalars. Its large-$N$ expansion is what has a gravity dual. For $d=3$ with a Chern–Simons term the paper defines it by a limit that also excludes monopole operators.

A gravitational theory in AdS with massless fields of every spin, $J=0,1,2,\dots$, including the graviton; Vasiliev's equations are its best-known form. It is conjectured (Klebanov–Polyakov) to be dual to the singlet sector of free or critical vector models.

defs.html: An approach to deriving higher-spin AdS/CFT, going back to Das and Jevicki, that rewrites a vector model in terms of its singlet bilinear $G(x_1,x_2)$ of two points and relates the pair of points, through conformal symmetry, to a point of AdS and a spin.

The singlet combination $G(x_1,x_2)=\frac1N\sum_I\phi^*_I(x_1)\phi_I(x_2)$ of the scalars at two points. Every $U(N)$-invariant observable can be written through it, and at large $N$ it fluctuates by $\eta/\sqrt N$ around the free propagator. With a gauge field it is not gauge invariant except at coincident points.

Symmetric tensor fields $\Phi_J$ of spin $J$ whose divergence and traces vanish. The paper's bulk theory consists of one such field for each spin, on a fixed AdS background; for massless fields, transversality can be read as a bulk gauge choice.

Said of an identity that holds inside the path integral, as an operator statement, rather than only at solutions of the equations of motion or inside correlators at separated points (on-shell). Coupling a dynamical gauge field to a current needs the current's map to the bulk off-shell.

The coefficient of a bulk field's leading power of the radial coordinate $z$ as $z\to0$. Here the boundary value of the spin-one bulk field $\Phi_1$ is its $z^0$ mode; in the QED dual it equals, up to normalisation, the boundary photon $A_i$.

A theory of $N$ fields in the vector representation of $U(N)$ or $O(N)$, solvable in $1/N$. The critical one adds $(\phi^*\phi)^2$ and flows to an interacting CFT, in which the scalar singlet has dimension 2 instead of the free $d-2$.

In three dimensions, the term $\propto k\int\varepsilon_{ijl}A_i\partial_jA_l$ for a gauge field, with integer level $k$. It is marginal and breaks parity. The paper keeps $\kappa=k/N$ fixed at large $N$, for the $U(1)$ photon and later for $U(N_c)$.

Local operators in a three-dimensional gauge theory that insert magnetic flux, charged under the topological $U(1)_T$ symmetry whose current is $*F$; in other $d$ they become codimension-3 operators. A Chern–Simons term at level $k$ gives them $k$ units of gauge charge.
Here, $N$ complex scalars in the fundamental representation of a $U(N_c)$ gauge field, studied at large $N$ with $N_c$ fixed, and in $d=3$ possibly with a Chern–Simons term. $N_c=1$ is scalar QED.

The three-dimensional Chern–Simons-matter theory of Aharony, Bergman and Jafferis, with gauge group $U(N)\times U(M)$, dual to M-theory on $AdS_4\times S^7/\mathbb Z_k$ and to type IIA strings. In a limit with $M\ll N$ it has a higher-spin regime.

The proposal (Chang, Minwalla, Sharma, Yin) that ABJ theory interpolates between Vasiliev higher-spin gravity, type IIA string theory and M-theory, so that a derived higher-spin dual could connect to strings.

The contact coupling $A_iA_i\,\phi^*\phi$ of two photons to two charged scalars, forced by gauge invariance of the kinetic term. At large $N$ its only role at leading order is to cancel a divergence in the photon self-energy.

Also the $\mathbb{CP}^{N-1}$ model: the conformal field theory reached in the infrared by $N$ scalars coupled to a $U(1)$ gauge field, with the Maxwell coupling $e$ and the quartic coupling $\lambda$ both sent to infinity. It is the low-energy scalar QED of this paper.

The family of gauges used for the photon: an average over gauges $\partial_iA_i=\omega$ with a non-local weight, labelled by a real $\zeta$, with $\zeta=1$ the Landau gauge. Unlike $R_\xi$ gauges it allows the limit $e\to\infty$ in the propagator directly.

The representations of the Euclidean conformal group with scaling dimension $\Delta=\frac d2+is$, $s$ real. They form a complete basis for suitable functions, so expansions in them are integrals over $\Delta$ along this line, deformed when a pole of interest lies off it.

The relation between conformal structures of dimension $\Delta$ and of the shadow dimension $\tilde\Delta=d-\Delta$, obtained by integrating against a two-point function. Because of it only half the coefficients along the principal series are independent.

The conformal three-point structures, labelled by $\Delta$, $J$ and a point $y$, used as a complete basis for functions of two points. They resemble three-point functions but are not correlators of any physical CFT.

Solutions $G_{\Delta,J}(x,z|y)$ of the AdS wave equation that approach a source at the boundary point $y$, behaving as $z^{\Delta-J}$. In the paper they double as the basis for expanding bulk fields, with the same coefficients as the bi-local.

In a vector model, said of a singlet operator bilinear in the fields, such as $\phi^*_I\phi^I$ or the conserved currents $\phi^*_I\partial\dots\partial\phi^I$; one for each spin. Each is dual to one bulk field $\Phi_J$.

A deformation by the square of a single-trace operator, here $(\phi^*\phi)^2$ written through $\sigma$. At large $N$ it does not change the bulk equations but the boundary condition of the dual bulk field, swapping its dimension $\Delta$ for $d-\Delta$.

For the bulk vector $\Phi_1$, the condition $\mathcal F_{ij}=0$ on the boundary field strength: its boundary value is fixed rather than fluctuating. It describes the free scalars, where the $U(1)$ is a global symmetry with a conserved current.

For the bulk vector $\Phi_1$, the condition $\mathcal F_{zi}=0$: the boundary value fluctuates and acts as a dynamical boundary gauge field. It describes low-energy QED without a Chern–Simons term, where the photon is that boundary value.

For the bulk vector in $AdS_4$, a linear combination of the electric and magnetic conditions, $\mathcal F_{ij}+\frac{2\pi i}{16\kappa}\varepsilon_{ijl}\mathcal F_{zl}=0$, set by the Chern–Simons ratio $\kappa=k/N$. It describes QED$_3$ with a Chern–Simons term.

The bulk-to-bulk propagator obeying the same equation as the physical one but the other boundary fall-off, that of the shadow dimension $d-\Delta$. Swapping one for the other is how a double-trace deformation or a gauging appears in the bulk.

Feynman diagrams of the bulk theory, drawn in AdS, whose external legs end on the boundary through bulk-to-boundary propagators. Their sum gives the CFT's correlation functions in the $1/N$ expansion.

questions.a: $d$ is the CFT's spacetime dimension, so the bulk is $AdS_{d+1}$, with radial coordinate $z$ vanishing at the boundary. $N$ counts the complex scalars; $e$ and $\lambda$ are the gauge and quartic couplings, rescaled by $N$ and sent to infinity for the CFT. $k$ is the Chern–Simons level in $d=3$, with $\kappa=k/N$ fixed. $\zeta$ labels the gauge-fixing ($\zeta=1$ is Landau gauge), and $J$ is the spin of the bulk field $\Phi_J$.

questions.q: Why is an off-shell map of local operators needed, when the on-shell one was already known?
questions.a: Gauging couples the dynamical photon to the $U(1)$ current inside the path integral, so the current must be replaced by its bulk counterpart as an operator identity, not just in correlators. The earlier work had such an identity only for spin zero below four dimensions. Section 3.2 supplies it for spin one, and indeed every spin, which turns the photon's coupling into a boundary coupling to $\Phi_1$.

questions.q: What is new compared with the authors' earlier derivation for free scalars?
questions.a: The earlier paper built the bi-local map and the bulk duals of the free and the critical vector model in $2<d<4$. New here are the off-shell map for every spin and for spin zero above four dimensions, the bulk dual of scalar QED with or without a Chern–Simons term, its extension to scalar QCD at fixed $N_c$, and the critical model's dual up to $d<6$.

questions.q: Why $2<d<4$ for QED but $2<d<6$ for the critical model?
questions.a: In $2<d<4$ the Maxwell term is irrelevant and the quartic coupling relevant, so scalar QED flows to an interacting CFT, believed to exist at large $N$ and, from lattice data, also at finite $N$ in $d=3$. The critical vector model is argued to exist at large $N$ for $2<d<6$, though above four dimensions it is unitary only in the $1/N$ expansion.

questions.q: How can gauging a boundary symmetry amount to just a change of boundary condition?
questions.a: In the free theory the bulk vector's $z^0$ mode is fixed, which is the electric condition: the $U(1)$ is global. In QED the photon $A_i$ couples linearly to the current, the boundary limit of $\Phi_1$, and at infinite gauge coupling acts as a Lagrange multiplier setting it to zero. The $z^0$ mode then fluctuates and equals $A_i$ up to normalisation: the magnetic condition.

questions.q: Why does the bulk propagator of $\Phi_1$ depend on how the CFT is gauge-fixed?
questions.a: The bulk fields are built from the bi-local $G(x_1,x_2)$, which is not gauge invariant: in the averaged gauges, $G$ at separated points stands for different operators. So bulk correlators away from the boundary inherit the CFT's gauge choice, and the vector's alternate boundary condition depends on $\zeta$. Gauge-invariant data come from the coincident limits, the local operators. The bulk vector itself has no gauge freedom.

questions.q: What does the Chern–Simons level do in the bulk?
questions.a: The Chern–Simons term involves only the photon, so it stays on the boundary. Combined with the photon's coupling to $\Phi_1$ it makes the boundary condition mixed, a combination of $\mathcal F_{ij}$ and $\mathcal F_{zl}$ set by $\kappa=k/N$; at $\kappa=0$ it is the magnetic condition of QED. The shadow propagator of $\Phi_1$ then comes in an infinite family labelled by $k$.

questions.q: Does the bulk theory contain monopole operators?
questions.a: Only without a Chern–Simons term. For $k\neq0$ a monopole carries $k$ units of gauge charge; the singlet sector is defined by gauging the scalars' $U(N)$ first, at infinite level, so any dressing that neutralises the monopole is charged under that gauging, and none survives. For $k=0$, and for $d\neq3$, monopoles are allowed, but the paper does not construct them; bulk solutions for them are proposed as future work.

questions.q: Is the bulk theory local, and is it Vasiliev's higher-spin gravity?
questions.a: Its quadratic term can be made local by choosing the normalisations $f_{\Delta,J}$, giving a fourth-order wave operator for each spin. The interactions remain non-local, and come with bulk counterterms. The authors believe the action is a gauge-fixed form of Vasiliev's theory on a fixed AdS background, since the spectrum is consistent, but this equivalence has not been shown.

questions.q: What is the second, negative propagator in the free two-point function?
questions.a: The free bulk two-point function is the difference of a massless propagator, the physical particle dual to a conserved current or to the dimension-$(d-2)$ scalar, and a massive one with negative sign. The latter is subleading near the boundary. Its spectrum matches the ghosts of a gauge-fixing of Vasiliev's theory, so the authors expect it to be a gauge-fixing ghost.

questions.q: Is the QED dual checked beyond leading order in $1/N$?
questions.a: By argument rather than computation. After a field redefinition $\sigma$ and the photon couple only linearly to the scalars, in the CFT and in the bulk. The difference between $\mathbb{CP}^{N-1}$ and free correlators is then built from free correlators joined by effective $\sigma$ and photon propagators, which identities turn into the same Witten diagrams with alternate boundary conditions, at any order.

questions.q: What does the paper not do?
questions.a: It works only in the $1/N$ expansion, and does not show that its bulk theory is Vasiliev's. It does not construct monopole solutions, nor include monopoles when there is a Chern–Simons term. Scalar QCD is sketched, not worked out, and only at fixed $N_c$; the large-$N_c$ Chern–Simons-matter limit, and with it fermions and ABJ theory, are left open. $d=4$ is not treated in detail.
